summaries.demographer: Miguel Perezramos is a 72-year-old married Puerto Rican man living with his wife Rosa in an owned, paid-off home in Spring, Texas, with no other full-time household members (Q51, Q55, Q58). He was born in Ponce, Puerto Rico, moved to the mainland in 1978, completed high school, and built a working life as a self-employed handyman before retirement (Q86, Q87, Q90, Q65). His household income is based on Social Security, Rosa's small pension, and occasional retirement savings withdrawals, placing him in a stable but cost-sensitive retired household (Q72, Q74, Q83). His social structure is multigenerational, with three adult children, six grandchildren, siblings in Puerto Rico and New Jersey, and strong church and senior center ties (Q05, Q06, Q07).
summaries.behavioral_economist: Miguel is highly loss-averse around household stability, health costs, and not becoming a burden to his children, which shapes his saving, repair, and spending behavior (Q61, Q62, Q83). He responds to uncertainty with routines, cash reserves, practical home maintenance, early voting, and relying on trusted family intermediaries for complex paperwork and information (Q23, Q36, Q42, Q50). His consumption choices are identity-rich: he will cut restaurants or hardware extras before cutting holiday food and family meals (Q59, Q81). He displays present-oriented generosity through food, favors, and volunteer repair work, balanced by cautious emergency planning (Q07, Q47, Q82).
summaries.political_scientist: Miguel is a moderate, weakly partisan Democrat whose civic behavior is anchored in voting, Catholic social concern, and practical local issues such as health care, flood control, roads, schools, and Social Security (Q23, Q24, Q95, Q96). He trusts doctors, pharmacists, parish health ministry, and family-vetted official sources more than social media, suggesting selective institutional trust rather than generalized distrust (Q42, Q48). His views on race and policing are reform-oriented and dignity-based, shaped by Latino experience, family conversations, and concern for Black Americans, though he does not participate in protests (Q26, Q27, Q28, Q29). His political identity is community-attached and pragmatic, with party alignment driven more by health care and respect for working families than ideological purity (Q24, Q95).
summaries.psychologist: Miguel presents as conscientious in practical domains, socially warm, nostalgic, and identity-driven, with self-worth tied to usefulness, family care, and cultural transmission (Q65, Q108, Q109). He experiences clinically meaningful anxiety that manifests as worry, forgetfulness, irritability, checking, and disorganization, but he has insight and uses counseling, walking, prayer, breathing, and household systems to cope (Q18, Q44, Q45, Q50). His emotional regulation is relational and sensory: Rosa, cooking, music, gardening, and church help stabilize him (Q43, Q47). He shows adaptive aging through accepting limits on ladders and heavy work while preserving competence through mentoring and storytelling (Q16, Q34, Q65, Q108).
